- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to account for potential rebound.
- Model frequently overshoots after recent price spikes (especially >75.00), leading to overcorrection; cap forecast at 2–3% below peak if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- Mean reversion is evident in 30d forecasts: if 10–15d average is >74.00, forecast should not exceed 74.50 unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 5d, model often fails to adjust; apply a 1–3% downward correction to next 3–5d forecast.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lagging sentiment shifts; if sentiment turns negative after 10d, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day for next 5d.
